foundation.audio — Zig migration branch
=======================================

Toolchain: Zig 0.17.0, pinned in ../.zig-version.
Default Android build: ../zig-build.gradle.kts, consuming separate FFmpeg DLLs/SOs.
No Cargo, cargo-ndk, bindgen, Rust FFmpeg wrappers, CPAL, Oboe or model runtime
is used by this build. Original Rust worktree files remain as a reference and
to preserve pre-existing uncommitted edits. They are not linked into the Zig library.

Implementation map
------------------
types / queue       -> src/queue.zig, engine.zig, protocol.zig
util / source       -> src/decoder.zig, file_io.zig, stream.zig, stream_decoder.zig
renderer            -> src/dsp.zig, ring.zig, loudness.zig, engine.zig
engine              -> src/engine.zig
cast remux          -> src/cast.zig
fabric-adapter      -> src/fabric.zig, source.zig, assets.zig, protocol.zig, transport.zig
jni-bridge          -> src/jni.zig
desktop C interface -> include/foundation_audio.h, src/root.zig

The device backend is miniaudio 0.11.25 (pinned source and license in vendor/).
device.c also contains small platform I/O and ARMv7 atomic-operation shims.
FFmpeg remains an external C dependency. Zig's explicit translate-c build step
imports its headers directly; switching languages does not remove FFmpeg itself.

Compatibility and verification boundary
---------------------------------------
Android JNI method names, parameter types, 32-byte status buffers and MFD1
metadata buffers are retained, including FabricRenderer and cast stream methods.
Pure Zig consumers use root.zig; non-Zig consumers can use the C header.
Rust-specific source APIs and async fabric-sdk traits are replaced by Zig APIs
and injected transport callbacks. A Rust application needs a C ABI adapter or
an updated consumer; this is not a source-compatible Cargo package replacement.
Fabric clock estimates still belong to the Fabric SDK and are injected through
protocol.Clock / Renderer.setClock; the JNI adapter retains identity-clock behavior.

AI/karaoke and music-analysis inference are intentionally disabled for this
migration. JNI compatibility methods report Off / no analysis data and load no
models. Offline model-training files are not altered.

Headless tests exercise decoding, resampling, seek, queue movement/shuffle,
crossfade math, silence timeline mapping, pause ramp, loudness, Matroska remux,
stream framing/cancellation, metadata, assets and protocol barriers. Android
build and symbol checks do not substitute for real-device playback, routing,
Bluetooth, latency, or end-to-end multi-device synchronization testing.
No Android device was connected during the migration.

The companion clef branch rewrite/zig-audio replaces the audio build with
compileAudioZig, invoking this repository's buildAndroidNative task and packaging
every .so under jniLibs/<abi>, plus build/generated/audioAssets. Its old
compileRustAndroid name is only a compatibility alias. Other Rust libraries in
clef are separate and keep their existing build. Consumers on other branches
must make the same change; invoking Cargo would overwrite the Zig JNI library.

Consumer verification: :app:compileAudioZig passed. Full native/assets merge is
blocked by the existing mixed AGP versions: clef 9.2.1 versus lyrics-ui 9.3.2.
The clef branch updates its Gradle wrapper to 9.5.0, required by lyrics-ui, but
does not change the application's unrelated AGP/Kotlin project configuration.
Windows shared-library C ABI playback, including a UTF-8 filename, passed.

FFmpeg distribution
-------------------
Android: ffmpeg-android-shared/<abi>, built from the exact FFmpeg submodule commit.
Windows: tools/build-ffmpeg-windows.ps1 builds ffmpeg-windows-shared using Zig CC.
The machine's pre-existing C:/Environments/Tools/ffmpeg build enables GPL and
version3; it is not the dependency to redistribute with this library.
Static fallback is disabled. On Windows, lib*.dll.a are DLL import stubs, not
archives containing the FFmpeg implementation. Android uses explicit lib*.so.

Run gradlew packageAudioDistribution for separate JNI/FFmpeg libraries, notices,
build parameters and corresponding FFmpeg source. Run tools/verify-native.py
to check all JNI exports, ELF dependencies, page alignment and provenance.
The application must carry the notices and provide matching sources as described
in FFMPEG-NOTICE.txt. Dynamic linking alone is not a blanket compliance guarantee.

Local build prerequisites
-------------------------
ZIG_EXE or zig.executable may select the pinned compiler.
Android NDK 29.0.14206865, minimum API 26.
Android FFmpeg rebuild currently uses the existing WSL/Linux-NDK dependency
builder on Windows, only when -PrebuildFfmpeg is explicitly supplied.
Ordinary Zig edits and incremental Android builds run on Windows directly.
